source.title: Statistical mechanics of support vector regression.

record.tranche_reason: Tests double descent in ε-SVR regression by sweeping sample load, rather than testing model-size or epoch sweeps in deep networks.
record.gate_note: The toy-model learning curves are the study's own results. The ResNet layer comparison measures decoding performance across layers, not test error over model size or epochs, so it is not recorded as a result for those versions. Double-descent findings cited from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study derives and simulates sample-wise learning curves for ridgeless ε-SVR on Gaussian toy data. It finds that generalization error peaks at effective load α̃=1 and that the tube size ε suppresses and shifts the peak. This is a new model class giving its own result on sample-wise double descent, not a deep-network replication, so T3 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that ε-SVR shows sample-wise double descent in generalization error at effective load α̃=1, and that ε acts as a regularizer that both suppresses and shifts the peak, like tuning effective model size. They also find that optimal ridge beats optimal ε-SVR, and that noise aligned with the coding direction worsens generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study derives and tests ε-SVR learning curves using statistical-mechanical analysis and toy regression experiments, rather than reproducing deep-network model-size, epoch, or sample-size experiments from the cited double-descent work.
record.method_sensitivity: The peak location and magnitude depend on ε; generalization also depends on noise strength and alignment with the coding direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimal ridge regression consistently gives lower generalization error than optimal ε-SVR across sample loads (Fig. 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under optimally tuned hyperparameters, ridge regularization generalizes better than ε-tube regularization in linear regression with noisy representations.

record.problems: The theoretical analysis assumes Gaussian representations and linear decoding. The empirical double-descent evidence is from a toy model; plotted curves provide no stated error bars or numerical values. The real-data ResNet experiment does not test double descent over model size or epochs.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying claim-version results left out. The ResNet layer experiment in Fig. 5 and Figs. S4–S5 was excluded because it compares decoding across layers rather than measuring double descent over model size, epochs, or sample count.

untested.parts: Only linear ε-SVR and ridge on Gaussian toy data; deep networks are not tested.
No capacity sweep; the only axis is sample load α=P/N. The ResNet experiment compares layers, not capacity.
The effective load α̃ is tested only along the sample axis, across ε. Size and epoch axes are not tested.
No label-noise sweep, no triple or multiple descent, and no explicit statement that the peak disappears under optimal λ or ε.
No re-plotting against an effective parameter count to check for a U shape.

missing.what: Theoretical result that above α̃=1 the generalization error is proportional to E∞ = βσ²/(1+βσ²). It therefore vanishes when noise strength σ or alignment β is zero, which bears on noise dependence of the curve.
Statement that generalization error typically diverges at the critical point α̃=1. This gives the strength of the sample-wise peak.

record.verdict_notes: All curves are figure-only, with no error bars. The V6 verdict rests on the authors' text about Fig. 3b. R14–R15 cannot show whether optimal regularization removes the peak, and the text does not say.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or test-error curve over increasing model size.
The study tests sample load in a toy regression setting, not whether adding data hurts near an interpolation threshold in deep networks.
Tests ε-SVR regression, including a toy model; does not test a range of other model classes.
Relates the sample-load transition to effective load; does not test a single complexity measure across size, epochs, and sample axes.
Studies effects of ε and representational noise geometry. It does not test multiple or triple descent, label-noise dependence, or whether the peak disappears under optimally tuned regularization.
No comparison with an effective parameter count or test of whether that recasts the curve as an ordinary U shape.
